# Repository audit — 7 October 2026

## Scope and baseline

Reviewed master `33a87f9`, all application JavaScript and CSS, the vendored
Backburner integration, manifest, packaging and lint scripts, dependency
lockfiles, the workflow and the only open PR, #3 (`11fb17d`). Changes build on
PR #3 without changing that branch, merging master or publishing a release.

PR #3's two latest quality runs and SonarCloud check passed. Its bootstrap tests
exercise only `444hu_comments.js`; its coverage threshold does not include the
modern or legacy injected frontend. Sonar's PR response reported 98.8% combined
coverage, 100% line coverage, 91.7% branch coverage and 70 lines to cover. Those
PR metrics are not proof of whole-application coverage. Master had no coverage
metric and its older analysis reported 13 bugs, 3 smells and no vulnerabilities
or hotspots. Existing issues include vendored findings, CSS diagnostics and
unhandled initialization promises. These are historical dashboard findings,
not 16 independently reproduced defects in today's code.

The active master ruleset requires a PR and the `quality` check, blocks force
pushes and deletion, requires zero approvals, and does not require the branch
to be current with master. No protection or secret settings were changed.

## Reproduced problems and fixes

| Problem                                                                                            | Effect                                                                   | Change                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Loader/application discovery happens outside retry protection; successful router path starts twice | Startup failures or duplicate route observers                            | Protect discovery and schedule one retry; return after success            |
| Custom forum names accept URL separators when pasted or restored                                   | A value such as `evil.example/#` can select a script host outside Disqus | Normalize and require a single subdomain; otherwise use the default forum |
| Temporary August 2022 forum is retained across navigation                                          | Later articles can load the outage forum                                 | Restore the configured/default forum before evaluating each article date  |
| Comment hash assumes an old `#comments` element                                                    | New article layouts throw when opening a comment link                    | Scroll the inserted wrapper and remove query/hash from the thread URL     |
| Pending initializations accumulate during rapid navigation                                         | Duplicate work and stale asynchronous initialization                     | Cancel pending timers and discard older initialization generations        |
| Geekz initializes its comment module before selecting the forum                                    | Module initialization sees an unset or old forum                         | Select the forum first                                                    |
| Async initialization promises lack rejection handling                                              | Failures can become unhandled rejections                                 | Handle and report failed initialization                                   |

The legacy replacement uses `textContent` to clear existing comments. This has
the same clearing purpose as `innerText` and works in both browsers and jsdom;
the original-code jsdom failure here is a DOM compatibility difference, not
proof that Chrome failed to clear comments.

## Tests and CI changes

Added 33 frontend DOM scenarios alongside the three bootstrap tests. Tests cover
router readiness failures, duplicate initialization, all existing insertion
methods, index pages, bounded insertion retries, comment hashes, Disqus loading
and forum switching, custom names, settings, navigation, outage dates, themes,
resizing, and legacy blog/Geekz behavior. Tests execute the actual sources and
the actual Backburner module in isolated VM contexts, without fetching Disqus.

Eight Python tests exercise packaging and baseline scripts as real subprocesses:
archive contents and integrity, undeclared asset exclusion, missing references,
unsafe paths, invalid versions, shifted lint findings, additional occurrences,
removed findings and analyzer failure.

The original frontend sources fail 17 of the new 33 scenarios; this includes
several scenarios for the same root cause and the jsdom compatibility difference
explained above. All scenarios pass with the fixes.

Coverage now includes all three application scripts with c8, which combines
repeated module executions into one LCOV record per file. CI enforces at least
85% lines, 80% functions and 75% branches **for each file**, uploads coverage
reports, enforces the already-clean formatting baseline, and waits for Sonar's
quality gate. The Sonar token is scoped to the steps that need it. Generated
reports and dependencies are ignored and excluded from Sonar source analysis.

Local coverage before remote CI:

| File            |  Lines | Branches | Functions |
| --------------- | -----: | -------: | --------: |
| Bootstrap       |   100% |   94.11% |      100% |
| Modern frontend | 92.90% |   84.86% |    95.65% |
| Legacy frontend |   100% |      96% |      100% |
| Total           | 94.69% |   87.11% |    96.87% |

These are c8/V8 source coverage values. Sonar counts executable lines and
conditions differently; its values must be reported separately.

The lint baseline check reports zero existing/current/new findings. Prettier
and JavaScript syntax checks pass. The build creates a validated 18-file ZIP;
only manifest-declared extension assets are included. The locked development
dependency audit reported zero known vulnerabilities when queried on this date.

## Remaining limits

No Chrome/Chromium executable is installed on this host. The tests establish
DOM behavior against representative fixtures, not live 444.hu/Ember, CSP,
Chrome extension loading, Disqus login, rendering or real network behavior.
The extension still depends on private Ember container APIs and page selectors;
site changes can break those assumptions. Router discovery retries indefinitely
while the site is unavailable, and unknown routes can wait five seconds before
being classified. Some error paths and historical football URL conversion are
not yet covered. These limits remain visible in the coverage report.

The manifest version remains `1.4.0.25`; the audit ZIP is a review build, not a
published release. PR #3 is a prerequisite of the audit branch. No store release,
merge, ruleset mutation or credential change is part of this audit.
